blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Handling a common cyber threat in practice is really about the first five minutes. A suspicious email arrives. An unusual alert pops up on your screen. A colleague reports that something strange is happening. What you do in those first five minutes decides whether the incident stays small or turns into something serious.

The rule of five minutes is simple. Stop what you are doing. Do not click anything else. Tell the security team immediately, and describe exactly what happened. Then wait for instructions before doing anything 'clever' on your own.

If we catch it in the first five minutes, we will almost certainly stop it from spreading. If we only catch it two hours later, we will spend the next two weeks investigating and explaining. The difference is not luck. It is the habit of reporting fast and resisting the urge to handle it alone.

items.q: According to the text, what mainly decides whether an incident stays small?
options: The size of the security team
What you do in the first five minutes
items.why: "What you do in those first five minutes decides whether the incident stays small or turns into something serious."

items.q: Which action is part of the rule of five minutes?
options: Turn off the whole network at once
Forward the email to your team so they can test it
Try to fix the problem quietly by yourself
Tell the security team immediately and describe what happened
items.why: "Tell the security team immediately, and describe exactly what happened."

items.q: What happens, according to the text, if the threat is only caught two hours later?
options: The security team is not needed
It takes weeks of investigating and explaining
The company loses no time at all
items.why: "we will spend the next two weeks investigating and explaining."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Reporting a threat quickly makes a real difference
A skilled employee should try to neutralise the threat alone
Cyber threats often start with something ordinary, like an email
Staying calm helps keep an incident small
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste em 'wait for instructions' e 'resisting the urge to handle it alone' — agir sozinho é justamente o que ele desaconselha.

items.q: The phrase "The difference is not luck" suggests that…
options: some companies are simply luckier than others
cyber threats are impossible to predict
good outcomes come from consistent habits, not chance
items.why: Inferência: se não é sorte, é 'the habit of reporting fast' — o resultado depende de comportamento, não de acaso.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver treinando um novo colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome to the team. Let me walk you through the one thing that matters most when a cyber threat shows up: the five-minute rule.

Last month we had a real case. Someone in finance got an email that looked exactly like a supplier invoice. Something felt slightly off, so she stopped, she didn't click the link, and she called us. Seven minutes from the moment it arrived. That was it. We blocked the sender, checked the systems, and the company stayed completely safe. No damage at all.

Now compare that with the opposite. If you decide to be clever and investigate on your own, you might click something, and then we lose the early warning. So here is what I need from you. If anything looks strange, stop straight away. Don't click, don't reply, don't forward it to a friend to check. Just tell us and describe what you saw.

Report fast and we will almost always contain it. Try to handle it alone and you turn five easy minutes into two hard weeks. It really is that simple.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the 'one thing that matters most', according to Oliver?
items.why: "the one thing that matters most… the five-minute rule."

items.q: In the real case Oliver describes, what did the person in finance do?
options: She stopped, didn't click, and called the security team
She clicked the link to check if it was safe
She deleted the email and said nothing
She forwarded the email to a colleague
items.why: "she stopped, she didn't click the link, and she called us."

items.q: How long did it take her to report the suspicious email?
items.why: "Seven minutes from the moment it arrived."

items.q: Why does Oliver warn against 'being clever' on your own?
options: Because it wastes the security team's budget
Because you might click something and lose the early warning
Because it breaks company rules about email
Because only managers are allowed to report threats
items.why: Inferência: 'you might click something, and then we lose the early warning' — agir sozinho destrói a vantagem dos primeiros minutos.

items.q: What does Oliver mean by "you turn five easy minutes into two hard weeks"?
options: A quick report prevents a long, difficult clean-up later
The training will take two weeks to finish
The security team needs two weeks' notice
items.why: Inferência: reportar rápido (5 min) evita o trabalho pesado de investigação (2 semanas) que vem depois de um atraso.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We trained everyone to handle a suspicious message calmly." To handle here means to…
items.why: To handle = lidar com / gerenciar uma situação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A warning ___ appeared on the screen, so she called the security team."
items.why: Alert = alerta, o aviso que apareceu na tela.

items.q: "A strange message can pop up at any moment." To pop up means to…
items.why: To pop up = surgir de repente na tela.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He resisted the ___ to fix the problem alone and reported it instead."
items.why: Urge = impulso; ele resistiu ao impulso de agir sozinho.

items.q: "If we act late, the threat can spread across the network." To spread means to…
items.why: To spread = espalhar-se, atingindo mais sistemas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre segurança e incidentes. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "When you spot something odd, flag it to the security team." To flag it means to…
items.why: Flag it = sinalizar, chamar a atenção para algo.

items.q: "The team managed to shut down the attack within minutes." To shut down means to…
items.why: Shut down = encerrar/parar algo por completo, como um ataque.

items.q: "We asked staff not to look into suspicious emails themselves." To look into means to…
items.why: Look into = investigar, examinar algo em detalhe.

items.q: "Reporting early helps us get ahead of the problem." To get ahead of means to…
options: deal with it before it grows
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se ao problema, agir antes que ele cresça.

items.q: "If everyone follows through on the five-minute rule, incidents stay small." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.
